prose_changes.old: Its books traveled. Translated into German, this Dutch practical divinity fed directly into German Pietism, and through the Dutch Reformed diaspora it reached South Africa and North America. The refuge culture left the wider mark. The Republic's habit of tolerating in private what it would not endorse in public, and its printing trade, put ideas into circulation across Europe that had nowhere else to go.

prose_changes.old: Both sides outlived the quarrel. The Remonstrant Brotherhood still exists as a small Dutch church, with its own seminary in Amsterdam. The Canons of Dort became one of the three confessional standards of the Dutch Reformed tradition worldwide, and the five points they answer are still taught in Reformed churches as the shorthand summary of Calvinism. 'Arminian', meanwhile, became a permanent label in English-language theology, taken up a century later by John Wesley and through him by the whole Methodist family.
prose_changes.new: Both sides outlived the quarrel. The Remonstrant Brotherhood still exists as a small Dutch church, with its own seminary in Amsterdam. The Canons of Dort became one of the three confessional standards of the Dutch Reformed tradition, sworn to by its ministers as far away as North America. 'Arminian', meanwhile, became a permanent label in English-language theology, taken up a century later by John Wesley and through him by the whole Methodist family.
prose_changes.reason: The 1840 constitution of the Reformed Dutch Church of North America has ministers subscribe the Heidelberg Catechism, the Belgic Confession and the Canons (lines 357-365), which supports the three standards and their reach. 'The five points they answer' are the Remonstrant articles, not Calvinism's summary, and the modern teaching use has no vendored or repo-cited source; the clause is removed.

prose_changes.old: The Waldensian Church still exists — since the nineteenth century out of the valleys and across Italy, with a sister church in Argentina and Uruguay, and since 1979 in union with Italian Methodists. Its valleys remain a place of pilgrimage for Protestants, and its sheer longevity made it a standing reference point for later Protestants looking for a church older than the Reformation.
prose_changes.new: The Waldensian Church still exists, and since the nineteenth century it has spread out of the valleys and across Italy. Its valleys remain a place of pilgrimage for Protestants, and its sheer longevity made it a standing reference point for later Protestants looking for a church older than the Reformation.

prose_changes.old: The Transylvanian church still exists, now the Hungarian Unitarian Church in Romania and Hungary, and is very likely the oldest continuously existing Unitarian body in the world. The Polish Brethren, expelled in 1658, scattered into the Netherlands and beyond, where their writings fed into Dutch and English rational theology and, at some distance, into later Unitarianism. Their argument for religious toleration — made by people with the most to lose from its absence — outlasted their communities.
prose_changes.new: The Transylvanian church still exists, now the Hungarian Unitarian Church in Romania and Hungary, and is very likely the oldest continuously existing Unitarian body in the world. The Polish Brethren, expelled in 1658, scattered into the Netherlands and beyond. In Holland many joined the Remonstrant and Mennonite churches and used the Dutch presses. Their writings may have fed Dutch and English rational theology, and at some distance later Unitarianism, though the trail is faint. Their argument for religious toleration — made by people with the most to lose from its absence — outlasted their communities.
prose_changes.reason: Rees (1818) shows the exiles merging into Remonstrant and Mennonite congregations and printing in Holland; that is stated. The wider influence rests on that one late history and on Belsham's naming, so it is qualified.
